meaningsEn: In the holy field of Kurukshetra
gathered together, desiring to fight
my sons and the sons of Pandu
what did they do, O Sanjaya?
meaningsTe: పుణ్యక్షేత్రమైన కురుక్షేత్రంలో
యుద్ధం చేయడానికి సిద్ధపడి చేరిన
నా కుమారులు మరియు పాండు కుమారులు
ఏమి చేశారు, ఓ సంజయా?

meaningsEn: After looking over the army
gathered by the sons of Pandu
King Duryodhana went to his
teacher and spoke these words.
meaningsTe: పాండవుల సైన్యాన్ని
చూసిన దుర్యోధన రాజు
తన ద్రోణాచార్య గురువు
దగ్గరకు వెళ్ళి .

meaningsEn: Thus addressed by Arjuna, Sri Krishna drew up the
best of chariots between the two armies, in full
view of Bhisma, Drona, and all the other kings, O
Dhrtarastra. He then said, "O Arjuna, behold these assembled Kauravas."
meaningsTe: : Thus addressed by Arjuna, Sri Krishna drew up
the best of chariots between the two armies, in full
view of Bhisma, Drona, and all the other kings, O
Dhrtarastra. He then said, "O Arjuna, behold these assembled Kauravas."

meaningsEn: n thus on the battlefield
Arjuna threw aside his bow and arrows
and sat down on the chariot seat
his heart overwhelmed with grief.
meaningsTe: : Having spoken thus on the battlefield
Arjuna threw aside his bow and arrows
and sat down on the chariot seat
his heart overwhelmed with grief.

meaningsEn: Seeing Arjuna full of compassion
his mind depressed
his eyes full of tears
Krishna spoke these words.
meaningsTe: కరుణతో నిండి
కన్నీళ్లు పెట్టుకుంటూ
విచారిస్తున్న అర్జునుడిని చూసి
కృష్ణుడు ఈ మాటలు పలికాడు.

meaningsEn: My dear Arjuna
how have these impurities
come upon you? They
are not at all befitting a brave man.
meaningsTe: అర్జునా
ఈ క్లిష్ట సమయంలో నీకు ఈ బలహీనత
ఎక్కడి నుండి వచ్చింది?
ఇది వీరులకు తగినది కాదు.

meaningsEn: Do not yield to
this weakness. It does
not befit you. Shake off
this small worry and arise!
meaningsTe: అర్జునా
బలహీనతకు లోనుకావద్దు
ఇది నీకు తగదు. నీ హృదయంలోని ఈ చిన్న బలహీనతను వదిలి పెట్టి
యుద్ధానికి సిద్ధంగా నిలబడు!

meaningsEn: How can I fight
against Bhishma and Drona
who are worthy
of my worship?
meaningsTe: ఓ కృష్ణా
నేను పూజించదగిన భీష్ముడిని మరియు
ద్రోణుడిని యుద్ధంలో
బాణాలతో ఎలా ఎదిరించగలను?

meaningsEn: It would be better to
live in this world by
begging than to enjoy life
by killing such noble teachers.
meaningsTe: గొప్పవారైన గురువులను చంపడం కంటే
ఈ లోకంలో భిక్షాటన చేస్తూ బ్రతకడం మేలు.
వారిని చంపి పొందే
భోగాలు రక్తంతో తడిసినవే అవుతాయి.

lines: yadvā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ
meaningsEn: Nor do we know which is better—conquering them or being
conquered by them. If we
killed the sons of Dhritarashtra
we should not care to live.
meaningsTe: మనకు ఏది మేలో తెలియడం లేదు మనం గెలవడమా లేక
వారు మనల్ని గెలవడమా? ఎవరిని
చంపి మనం బ్రతకాలని అనుకోవడం లేదో
ఆ ధృతరాష్ట్రుని కుమారులే మన ముందు నిలబడి ఉన్నారు.

meaningsEn: I am confused about my duty.
Tell me for certain what is best.
I am Your disciple.
Please instruct me.
meaningsTe: కర్తవ్యం పట్ల నాకు సందేహం కలుగుతోంది. ఏది
శ్రేయస్కరమో నాకు ఖచ్చితంగా
చెప్పు. నేను నీ శిష్యుడిని
నన్ను శాసించు.

meaningsEn: Even if I were to win unchallenged sovereignty of
a prosperous earth or even lordship over the Devas
I do not feel that it would
dispel the grief that withers up my senses.
meaningsTe: Even if I were to win unchallenged sovereignty of
a prosperous earth or even lordship over the Devas
I do not feel that it would
dispel the grief that withers up my senses.

meaningsEn: Having thus spoken to Sri Krsna,
Arjuna, the conqueror of sleep and
the scorcher of foes, said, "I
will not fight," and became silent.
meaningsTe: Having thus spoken to Sri Krsna,
Arjuna, the conqueror of sleep and
the scorcher of foes, said, "I
will not fight," and became silent.

meaningsEn: O King
to him who was thus sorrowing between the two armies
Sri Krishna spoke the following words
as if smiling (by way of ridicule).
meaningsTe: O King
to him who was thus sorrowing between the two armies
Sri Krishna spoke the following words
as if smiling (by way of ridicule).

meaningsEn: Wise people
do not worry
about the living
or the dead.
meaningsTe: అర్జునా
నువ్వు విచారించకూడని వాటి కోసం విచారిస్తున్నావు.
జ్ఞానులు జీవించి ఉన్నవారి గురించి కానీ
మరణించిన వారి గురించి కానీ దుఃఖించరు.

meaningsEn: There never was a time when I did not exist
nor you
nor any of these kings. Nor will there be any time
in the future when all of us shall cease to exist.
meaningsTe: There never was a time when I did not exist
nor you
nor any of these kings. Nor will there be any time
in the future when all of us shall cease to exist.

meaningsEn: As the soul passes from
boyhood to youth to old age
it passes into
another body at death.
meaningsTe: ఈ దేహంలో ఉన్న జీవుడికి బాల్యం
యవ్వనం
ముసలితనం ఎలా కలుగుతాయో
మరణం తర్వాత మరో దేహాన్ని పొందడం కూడా అలాగే జరుగుతుంది.

meaningsEn: The contact of the senses with their objects,
O Arjuna, gives rise to feelings of cold
and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and
go, never lasting long. Endure them, O Arjuna.
meaningsTe: The contact of the senses with their objects,
O Arjuna, gives rise to feelings of cold
and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and
go, never lasting long. Endure them, O Arjuna.

meaningsEn: For
he whom these do not affect
O chief of men
and to whom pain and pleasure are equal - that steadfast man alone is worthy of immortality.
meaningsTe: For
he whom these do not affect
O chief of men
and to whom pain and pleasure are equal - that steadfast man alone is worthy of immortality.

meaningsEn: The unreal never comes into being
the real never ceases
to be. The truth
about these two is seen by the seers.
meaningsTe: The unreal never comes into being
the real never ceases
to be. The truth
about these two is seen by the seers.

meaningsEn: Know that to be indestructible
by which all this is
pervaded. No one can cause
the destruction of this immutable.
meaningsTe: Know that to be indestructible
by which all this is
pervaded. No one can cause
the destruction of this immutable.

meaningsEn: These bodies of the Jiva (the embodied
self) are said to have an end,
while the Jiva itself is eternal, indestructible,
and incomprehensible. Therefore, fight, O Bharata (Arjuna).
meaningsTe: These bodies of the Jiva (the embodied
self) are said to have an end,
while the Jiva itself is eternal, indestructible,
and incomprehensible. Therefore, fight, O Bharata (Arjuna).

meaningsEn: He who considers It (the self) to be the slayer
and he who thinks of
It as slain—both are ignorant. For
the self neither slays nor is being slain.
meaningsTe: He who considers It (the self) to be the slayer
and he who thinks of
It as slain—both are ignorant. For
the self neither slays nor is being slain.

lines: nāyaṁ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ
meaningsEn: For the soul
there is neither
birth nor death. He is unborn
eternal and ever-existing.
meaningsTe: ఆత్మకు ఎప్పుడూ పుట్టుక కానీ
మరణం కానీ ఉండవు. అది పుట్టనిది
నిత్యమైనది
శాశ్వతమైనది. శరీరం నశించినా అది నశించదు.

meaningsEn: He who knows this self to
be indestructible, unborn, unchanging, and thus eternal—how,
O Arjuna, does he cause anyone to
be killed, and whom does he kill?
meaningsTe: He who knows this self to
be indestructible, unborn, unchanging, and thus eternal—how,
O Arjuna, does he cause anyone to
be killed, and whom does he kill?

meaningsEn: As a man casts off worn
out garments and puts on new ones
so does the embodied self cast off its
worn out bodies and enter into new ones.
meaningsTe: As a man casts off worn
out garments and puts on new ones
so does the embodied self cast off its
worn out bodies and enter into new ones.

meaningsEn: Weapons cannot cleave It
fire cannot burn It
waters cannot wet It
and wind cannot dry It.
meaningsTe: Weapons cannot cleave It
fire cannot burn It
waters cannot wet It
and wind cannot dry It.

meaningsEn: It cannot be cleaved; It cannot
be burned; It cannot be wetted,
and It cannot be dried; It is
eternal, all pervasive, stable, immovable, and primordial.
meaningsTe: It cannot be cleaved; It cannot
be burned; It cannot be wetted,
and It cannot be dried; It is
eternal, all pervasive, stable, immovable, and primordial.

meaningsEn: This (self) is said to be
unmanifest, inconceivable, and unchanging. Therefore,
knowing it thus, it does
not befit you to grieve.
meaningsTe: This (self) is said to be
unmanifest, inconceivable, and unchanging. Therefore,
knowing it thus, it does
not befit you to grieve.

meaningsEn: Or
if you consider this self as constantly being born and constantly dying
O mighty-armed one
it still does not become you to feel grief.
meaningsTe: Or
if you consider this self as constantly being born and constantly dying
O mighty-armed one
it still does not become you to feel grief.

meaningsEn: For
death is certain for the born
and rebirth is certain for the dead; therefore
you should not grieve for what is inevitable.
meaningsTe: For
death is certain for the born
and rebirth is certain for the dead; therefore
you should not grieve for what is inevitable.

meaningsEn: O Arjuna
beings have an unknown beginning
a known middle
and an unknown end. What is there to grieve about in all this?
meaningsTe: O Arjuna
beings have an unknown beginning
a known middle
and an unknown end. What is there to grieve about in all this?

meaningsEn: One regards This (self) as a wonder;
another speaks of It as a wonder;
yet another hears of It as a wonder; and even after hearing of It
one does not know It.
meaningsTe: One regards This (self) as a wonder;
another speaks of It as a wonder;
yet another hears of It as a wonder; and even after hearing of It
one does not know It.

meaningsEn: The self in the body
O Arjuna
is eternal and indestructible. This is the case for all selves in all bodies. Therefore
it is not fitting for you to feel grief for any being.
meaningsTe: The self in the body
O Arjuna
is eternal and indestructible. This is the case for all selves in all bodies. Therefore
it is not fitting for you to feel grief for any being.

meaningsEn: Further, considering also your own duty,
it does not befit you to
waver. For, to a Kshatriya, there is
no greater good than a righteous war.
meaningsTe: Further, considering also your own duty,
it does not befit you to
waver. For, to a Kshatriya, there is
no greater good than a righteous war.

meaningsEn: Happy are the Ksatriyas
O Arjuna
to whom such a war comes of its
own accord; it opens the gates to heaven.
meaningsTe: Happy are the Ksatriyas
O Arjuna
to whom such a war comes of its
own accord; it opens the gates to heaven.

meaningsEn: But if you do not fight this righteous war
you will be turning away
from your duty and honor
and will incur sin.
meaningsTe: But if you do not fight this righteous war
you will be turning away
from your duty and honor
and will incur sin.

meaningsEn: Further
people will speak ill of you for all time
and for one accustomed to being honored
dishonor is worse than death.
meaningsTe: Further
people will speak ill of you for all time
and for one accustomed to being honored
dishonor is worse than death.

meaningsEn: The great warriors will think that
you have fled from battle out of
fear. Those who held you in high
esteem will now speak of you disparagingly.
meaningsTe: The great warriors will think that
you have fled from battle out of
fear. Those who held you in high
esteem will now speak of you disparagingly.

meaningsEn: Your enemies
slandering your prowess
will use words that should never be
uttered. What could be more painful than that?
meaningsTe: Your enemies
slandering your prowess
will use words that should never be
uttered. What could be more painful than that?

meaningsEn: If slain, you will win heaven;
or if victorious, you will
enjoy the earth. Therefore, arise,
O Arjuna, resolved to fight.
meaningsTe: If slain, you will win heaven;
or if victorious, you will
enjoy the earth. Therefore, arise,
O Arjuna, resolved to fight.

meaningsEn: Holding pleasure and pain, gain and loss,
victory and defeat as equal, gird
yourself up for the battle. Thus,
you shall not incur any sin.
meaningsTe: Holding pleasure and pain, gain and loss,
victory and defeat as equal, gird
yourself up for the battle. Thus,
you shall not incur any sin.

meaningsEn: This Buddhi concerning the Self (Sankhya) has been imparted
to you. Now listen to this with regard to Yoga
by following which you will get
rid of the bondage of Karma.
meaningsTe: This Buddhi concerning the Self (Sankhya) has been imparted
to you. Now listen to this with regard to Yoga
by following which you will get
rid of the bondage of Karma.

meaningsEn: Here
there is no loss of effort
nor any accrual of evil. Even a little of this
Dharma (called Karma Yoga) protects one from the great fear.
meaningsTe: Here
there is no loss of effort
nor any accrual of evil. Even a little of this
Dharma (called Karma Yoga) protects one from the great fear.

meaningsEn: In this (Karma Yoga)
O Arjuna
the resolute mind is single pointed; the minds
of the irresolute are multi branched and endless.
meaningsTe: In this (Karma Yoga)
O Arjuna
the resolute mind is single pointed; the minds
of the irresolute are multi branched and endless.

meaningsEn: - O Partha, the unwise, who rejoice in the letter of the Vedas, say, "There is nothing else." They are full only of worldly desires and they hanker for heaven.
They speak flowery words that offer mirth as the fruit of work.
They look upon the Vedas as consisting entirely of varied rites for the attainment of pleasure and power.
Those who cling so to pleasure and power are attracted by that speech (offering heavenly rewards) and are unable to develop the resolute will of a concentrated mind.

Those who cling so to pleasure and power are attracted by that speech (offering heavenly rewards) and are unable to develop the resolute will of a concentrated mind.

meaningsEn: - O Partha, the unwise, who rejoice in the letter of the Vedas, say, "There is nothing else." They are full only of worldly desires and they yearn for heaven.
They speak flowery words that offer mirth as the fruit of work.
They view the Vedas as consisting entirely of varied rites for the attainment of pleasure and power.
Those who cling so to pleasure and power are attracted by that speech (offering heavenly rewards) and are unable to develop the resolute will of a focused mind.

meaningsEn: The Vedas have the three Gunas as their sphere
O Arjuna. You must be free from the three Gunas and be free from the pairs of
opposites. Abide in pure Sattva; never care to acquire things and to protect what has been acquired
but be established in the Self.
meaningsTe: The Vedas have the three Gunas as their sphere
O Arjuna. You must be free from the three Gunas and be free from the pairs of
opposites. Abide in pure Sattva; never care to acquire things and to protect what has been acquired
but be established in the Self.

meaningsEn: What use does a thirsty person have
for a water reservoir when all sides of
it are flooded—that is the only use of
all the Vedas for a Brahmana who knows.
meaningsTe: What use does a thirsty person have
for a water reservoir when all sides of
it are flooded—that is the only use of
all the Vedas for a Brahmana who knows.

meaningsEn: Focus on your duty
not the result. Don't
be attached
to inaction.
meaningsTe: కర్తవ్యాన్ని నిర్వహించు
ఫలితాన్ని ఆశించకు. పని
చేయకుండా
సోమరిగా ఉండవద్దు.

meaningsEn: Abandoning attachment and established in Yoga
perform works
viewing success and failure with an even mind.
Evenness of mind is said to be Yoga.
meaningsTe: Abandoning attachment and established in Yoga
perform works
viewing success and failure with an even mind.
Evenness of mind is said to be Yoga.

meaningsEn: Action done with attachment
O Arjuna
is far inferior to action done with evenness of mind. Seek refuge in
evenness of mind; those who act with a motive for results are miserable.
meaningsTe: Action done with attachment
O Arjuna
is far inferior to action done with evenness of mind. Seek refuge in
evenness of mind; those who act with a motive for results are miserable.

meaningsEn: A person with an evenness of mind discards
both good and evil here and now. Therefore
strive for Yoga; for
Yoga is skill in action.
meaningsTe: A person with an evenness of mind discards
both good and evil here and now. Therefore
strive for Yoga; for
Yoga is skill in action.

meaningsEn: The wise, who possess evenness of mind,
relinquish the fruits born of action, and
are freed from the bondage of birth,
going to the region beyond all ills.
meaningsTe: The wise, who possess evenness of mind,
relinquish the fruits born of action, and
are freed from the bondage of birth,
going to the region beyond all ills.

meaningsEn: When your intellect has passed
beyond the tangle of delusion
you will yourself feel disgusted with what
you have heard and what you will hear.
meaningsTe: When your intellect has passed
beyond the tangle of delusion
you will yourself feel disgusted with what
you have heard and what you will hear.

meaningsEn: When your intellect
having been well enlightened by hearing from Me and firmly placed
stands unshaken in a concentrated mind
then you will attain the vision of the Self.
meaningsTe: When your intellect
having been well enlightened by hearing from Me and firmly placed
stands unshaken in a concentrated mind
then you will attain the vision of the Self.

meaningsEn: What is the mode of speech of one who is of firm wisdom, established in the control of the mind?
What does a man of firm wisdom speak, O Krsna?
How does he sit?
How does he move?"
meaningsTe: What is the mode of speech of one who is of firm wisdom, established in the control of the mind?
What does a man of firm wisdom speak, O Krsna?
How does he sit?
How does he move?"

meaningsEn: The Lord said
"When a man renounces all the desires
of the mind and is content with himself
then he is said to possess firm wisdom."
meaningsTe: The Lord said
"When a man renounces all the desires
of the mind and is content with himself
then he is said to possess firm wisdom."

meaningsEn: He whose mind is not perturbed by pain,
who has no longing for pleasures, who
is free from desire, fear, and anger—he
is called a sage of firm wisdom.
meaningsTe: He whose mind is not perturbed by pain,
who has no longing for pleasures, who
is free from desire, fear, and anger—he
is called a sage of firm wisdom.

meaningsEn: He who has no love on any side
who
upon finding good or evil
neither rejoices nor hates—his wisdom is firmly set.
meaningsTe: He who has no love on any side
who
upon finding good or evil
neither rejoices nor hates—his wisdom is firmly set.

meaningsEn: When one is able to draw their senses
away from the objects of sense on all sides
like a tortoise draws in its limbs
then their wisdom is firmly established.
meaningsTe: When one is able to draw their senses
away from the objects of sense on all sides
like a tortoise draws in its limbs
then their wisdom is firmly established.

meaningsEn: The objects of the senses, except for the pleasure
they bring, turn away from the abstinent dweller in
the body. Even the pleasure turns away from him when
the Self, which is supreme over the senses, is seen.
meaningsTe: The objects of the senses, except for the pleasure
they bring, turn away from the abstinent dweller in
the body. Even the pleasure turns away from him when
the Self, which is supreme over the senses, is seen.

meaningsEn: The turbulent senses
O Arjuna
can forcibly carry away the mind of even a wise man
though he is ever striving.
meaningsTe: The turbulent senses
O Arjuna
can forcibly carry away the mind of even a wise man
though he is ever striving.

meaningsEn: Having controlled all the senses
let him remain in contemplation
regarding Me as supreme; for his knowledge is
firmly established when his senses are under control.
meaningsTe: Having controlled all the senses
let him remain in contemplation
regarding Me as supreme; for his knowledge is
firmly established when his senses are under control.

meaningsEn: To one who is thinking about sense-objects
attachment to them arises;
from attachment arises desire
and from desire arises anger.
meaningsTe: To one who is thinking about sense-objects
attachment to them arises;
from attachment arises desire
and from desire arises anger.

meaningsEn: Anger leads to delusion
which causes the loss of memory; the loss of memory leads to the destruction of discrimination
and with the destruction of discrimination
one is lost.
meaningsTe: Anger leads to delusion
which causes the loss of memory; the loss of memory leads to the destruction of discrimination
and with the destruction of discrimination
one is lost.

meaningsEn: But he who goes through the sense objects
with the senses free from love and hate
disciplined and controlled
attains serenity.
meaningsTe: But he who goes through the sense objects
with the senses free from love and hate
disciplined and controlled
attains serenity.

meaningsEn: In that serenity
all sorrow is lost; for in the
case of the person with a serene mind
the Buddhi is quickly established.
meaningsTe: In that serenity
all sorrow is lost; for in the
case of the person with a serene mind
the Buddhi is quickly established.

meaningsEn: There is no Buddhi for the unintegrated, nor is
there contemplation of the self for him, and without
contemplation of the self, there is no peace; and
for one who lacks peace, where is the happiness?
meaningsTe: There is no Buddhi for the unintegrated, nor is
there contemplation of the self for him, and without
contemplation of the self, there is no peace; and
for one who lacks peace, where is the happiness?

meaningsEn: For, when the mind follows the senses,
experiencing their objects, his understanding is carried
away by them, just as the wind
carries away a ship on the waters.
meaningsTe: For, when the mind follows the senses,
experiencing their objects, his understanding is carried
away by them, just as the wind
carries away a ship on the waters.

meaningsEn: Therefore
O mighty-armed one
he whose senses are restrained from going after their objects on all sides
his wisdom is firmly established.
meaningsTe: Therefore
O mighty-armed one
he whose senses are restrained from going after their objects on all sides
his wisdom is firmly established.

meaningsEn: What is night for all beings
in it the one who is controlled
is awake; when all beings are awake
that is the night for the sage who sees.
meaningsTe: What is night for all beings
in it the one who is controlled
is awake; when all beings are awake
that is the night for the sage who sees.

meaningsEn: He into whom all desires enter
just as the waters enter the full and undisturbed sea
attains peace
and not he who longs after objects of desire.
meaningsTe: He into whom all desires enter
just as the waters enter the full and undisturbed sea
attains peace
and not he who longs after objects of desire.

meaningsEn: The one who, abandoning
all desires, abides without longing,
possession, and the sense of
'I' and 'mine', wins peace.
meaningsTe: The one who, abandoning
all desires, abides without longing,
possession, and the sense of
'I' and 'mine', wins peace.

meaningsEn: This is the Brahmic state
O Arjuna. No one attaining to this is deluded. By
abiding in this state even at the hour of death
one will attain the Self.
meaningsTe: This is the Brahmic state
O Arjuna. No one attaining to this is deluded. By
abiding in this state even at the hour of death
one will attain the Self.

meaningsEn: if you deem knowledge
to be superior to action
why then do you urge me
to engage in this terrible deed?"
meaningsTe: if you deem knowledge
to be superior to action
why then do you urge me
to engage in this terrible deed?"

meaningsEn: You confuse my mind with statements
that seem to contradict each other; tell
me for certain the one way by
which I could reach the highest good.
meaningsTe: You confuse my mind with statements
that seem to contradict each other; tell
me for certain the one way by
which I could reach the highest good.

meaningsEn: Jnana Yoga
for the Sankhyas
and Karma Yoga
for the Yogins."
meaningsTe: The Lord said, "In this world, a two fold way
was of yore laid down by Me, O sinless one
Jnana Yoga for the Sankhyas
and Karma Yoga for the Yogins."

meaningsEn: No one experiences freedom from
action (Naiskarmya) by abstaining from
work; and no one ever attains
success through mere renunciation of work.
meaningsTe: No one experiences freedom from
action (Naiskarmya) by abstaining from
work; and no one ever attains
success through mere renunciation of work.

meaningsEn: No one can remain still for even a moment
without doing work; for everyone is compelled to act
despite themselves
by the Gunas born of Nature.
meaningsTe: No one can remain still for even a moment
without doing work; for everyone is compelled to act
despite themselves
by the Gunas born of Nature.

meaningsEn: He who
controlling the organs of action
lets his mind dwell on the objects of the senses
is a deluded person and a hypocrite.
meaningsTe: He who
controlling the organs of action
lets his mind dwell on the objects of the senses
is a deluded person and a hypocrite.

meaningsEn: But he who, subduing his senses by
the mind, O Arjuna, begins to practice
Karma Yoga through the organs of action
and who is free from attachment, excels.
meaningsTe: But he who, subduing his senses by
the mind, O Arjuna, begins to practice
Karma Yoga through the organs of action
and who is free from attachment, excels.

meaningsEn: You must perform your obligatory
action; for action is superior
to non action (Jñāna Yoga). For a person following non action
not even the sustenance of the body is possible.
meaningsTe: You must perform your obligatory
action; for action is superior
to non action (Jñāna Yoga). For a person following non action
not even the sustenance of the body is possible.

meaningsEn: This world is held in the bondage of work only
when work is not performed as a sacrifice. O Arjuna
you must perform work for this purpose
free from attachment.
meaningsTe: This world is held in the bondage of work only
when work is not performed as a sacrifice. O Arjuna
you must perform work for this purpose
free from attachment.

meaningsEn: In the beginning
the Lord of all beings created man along with the sacrifice and said
"By this shall you prosper; this shall be the cow of plenty
granting all your desires."
meaningsTe: In the beginning
the Lord of all beings created man along with the sacrifice and said
"By this shall you prosper; this shall be the cow of plenty
granting all your desires."

meaningsEn: By this, please the gods,
and they will support you.
Thus, nourishing each other, you
may obtain the highest good.
meaningsTe: By this, please the gods,
and they will support you.
Thus, nourishing each other, you
may obtain the highest good.

meaningsEn: The gods
pleased by the sacrifice
will bestow upon you the enjoyments you desire. He who enjoys the bounty
of the gods without giving them anything in return is but a thief.
meaningsTe: The gods
pleased by the sacrifice
will bestow upon you the enjoyments you desire. He who enjoys the bounty
of the gods without giving them anything in return is but a thief.

meaningsEn: Pious people who eat the remnants
of sacrifices are freed from all sins
whereas those who are sinful and cook only
for their own sake will only incur sin.
meaningsTe: Pious people who eat the remnants
of sacrifices are freed from all sins
whereas those who are sinful and cook only
for their own sake will only incur sin.

meaningsEn: All beings arise from food
food is produced from rain
rain comes from sacrifice
and sacrifice is born of action.
meaningsTe: All beings arise from food
food is produced from rain
rain comes from sacrifice
and sacrifice is born of action.

meaningsEn: Know that activity springs from Brahman
i.e.
the physical body; Brahman arises from the imperishable Self; therefore
the all-pervading Brahman is ever established in sacrifice.
meaningsTe: Know that activity springs from Brahman
i.e.
the physical body; Brahman arises from the imperishable Self; therefore
the all-pervading Brahman is ever established in sacrifice.

meaningsEn: He who does not follow the wheel thus set in motion here
lives in sin
satisfying the senses
O Arjuna; he lives in vain.
meaningsTe: He who does not follow the wheel thus set in motion here
lives in sin
satisfying the senses
O Arjuna; he lives in vain.

meaningsEn: But the man whose delight is only in the Self
who is satisfied with the Self
who rejoices in the Self
for him nothing remains to be accomplished.
meaningsTe: But the man whose delight is only in the Self
who is satisfied with the Self
who rejoices in the Self
for him nothing remains to be accomplished.

meaningsEn: He has no purpose to gain
from work done or left undone
nor does he have
to rely on any end.
meaningsTe: He has no purpose to gain
from work done or left undone
nor does he have
to rely on any end.

meaningsEn: Therefore
do your work without attachment
which ought to be done. For
a person who works without attachment attains the Supreme.
meaningsTe: Therefore
do your work without attachment
which ought to be done. For
a person who works without attachment attains the Supreme.

meaningsEn: Indeed
Janaka and others reached perfection through Karma Yoga
alone. Even recognizing its necessity for guiding the world
you must perform action.
meaningsTe: Indeed
Janaka and others reached perfection through Karma Yoga
alone. Even recognizing its necessity for guiding the world
you must perform action.

meaningsEn: Whatever a great man does
others do too.
Whatever standard he sets
the world follows it.
meaningsTe: Whatever a great man does
others do too.
Whatever standard he sets
the world follows it.

meaningsEn: For me
Arjuna
there is nothing in all the three worlds that ought to be done
nor is there anything unaccomplished that ought to be accomplished. Yet I continue to work.
meaningsTe: For me
Arjuna
there is nothing in all the three worlds that ought to be done
nor is there anything unaccomplished that ought to be accomplished. Yet I continue to work.

meaningsEn: If I did not
continue to work unweariedly
O Arjuna
people would follow my path.
meaningsTe: If I did not
continue to work unweariedly
O Arjuna
people would follow my path.

meaningsEn: If I do not do the work
these people will be lost; and I will be
causing chaos in life and
thereby ruining all these people.
meaningsTe: If I do not do the work
these people will be lost; and I will be
causing chaos in life and
thereby ruining all these people.

meaningsEn: Just as the ignorant, attached to their
work, act, O Arjuna, so too the
learned should act without any attachment, and
only for the welfare of the world.
meaningsTe: Just as the ignorant, attached to their
work, act, O Arjuna, so too the
learned should act without any attachment, and
only for the welfare of the world.

meaningsEn: He should not bewilder the minds of
the ignorant who are attached to work; rather
he should himself perform work with devotion
and cause others to do the same.
meaningsTe: He should not bewilder the minds of
the ignorant who are attached to work; rather
he should himself perform work with devotion
and cause others to do the same.

meaningsEn: Actions are being performed in every way by the Gunas of Prakrti; he whose nature is deluded by egoism
however
thinks
'I am the doer.'
meaningsTe: Actions are being performed in every way by the Gunas of Prakrti; he whose nature is deluded by egoism
however
thinks
'I am the doer.'

meaningsEn: But he who knows the truth about the division of the Gunas and works
O mighty-armed one
through his knowledge that the Gunas 'operate
on their own products,' is not attached.
meaningsTe: But he who knows the truth about the division of the Gunas and works
O mighty-armed one
through his knowledge that the Gunas 'operate
on their own products,' is not attached.

meaningsEn: Those who are deluded by the Gunas of Prakrti
are attached to the works of the Gunas. But
he who knows the whole truth should not disturb
the ignorant who do not know the whole truth.
meaningsTe: Those who are deluded by the Gunas of Prakrti
are attached to the works of the Gunas. But
he who knows the whole truth should not disturb
the ignorant who do not know the whole truth.

meaningsEn: Surrender all your actions to Me
with a mind focused on the Self
free from desire and selfishness
and fight with the heat of excitement abated.
meaningsTe: Surrender all your actions to Me
with a mind focused on the Self
free from desire and selfishness
and fight with the heat of excitement abated.

meaningsEn: Those men who
full of faith
ever practice this teaching of Mine and those who
receive it without cavil—even they are released from karma.
meaningsTe: Those men who
full of faith
ever practice this teaching of Mine and those who
receive it without cavil—even they are released from karma.

meaningsEn: But those who slander it
and those who do not practice this teaching of Mine—know
them to be utterly senseless and devoid of all knowledge
and thus lost.
meaningsTe: But those who slander it
and those who do not practice this teaching of Mine—know
them to be utterly senseless and devoid of all knowledge
and thus lost.

meaningsEn: Even the man of knowledge
acts according to his nature;
all beings follow their own
nature. What will repression accomplish?
meaningsTe: Even the man of knowledge
acts according to his nature;
all beings follow their own
nature. What will repression accomplish?

meaningsEn: Each sense has a fixed attachment
to and aversion for its corresponding object
but one should not come under their sway
for they are enemies.
meaningsTe: Each sense has a fixed attachment
to and aversion for its corresponding object
but one should not come under their sway
for they are enemies.

meaningsEn: Better is one's own duty
even if done poorly
than the duty of another done well. It is better to die
while performing one's own duty; the duty of another is full of fear.
meaningsTe: Better is one's own duty
even if done poorly
than the duty of another done well. It is better to die
while performing one's own duty; the duty of another is full of fear.

meaningsEn: But, O Krsna, what
impels one to commit sin,
even against their own will,
as if constrained by force?"
meaningsTe: But, O Krsna, what
impels one to commit sin,
even against their own will,
as if constrained by force?"

meaningsEn: The Lord said, "It is desire, it
is wrath, born of the guna of rajas;
it is a great devourer, an impeller of
sin. Know this to be the enemy here."
meaningsTe: The Lord said, "It is desire, it
is wrath, born of the guna of rajas;
it is a great devourer, an impeller of
sin. Know this to be the enemy here."

meaningsEn: As a fire is enveloped by smoke
as a mirror is covered by dust
and as an embryo is encased in the amniotic sac
so is this world enveloped by desire.
meaningsTe: As a fire is enveloped by smoke
as a mirror is covered by dust
and as an embryo is encased in the amniotic sac
so is this world enveloped by desire.

meaningsEn: The knowledge of the intelligent self is enveloped by this constant enemy
O Arjuna
which is of the nature of desire
and is difficult to gratify and insatiable.
meaningsTe: The knowledge of the intelligent self is enveloped by this constant enemy
O Arjuna
which is of the nature of desire
and is difficult to gratify and insatiable.

meaningsEn: The senses, the mind, and
the intellect are said to be
its instruments; by these, it overpowers
the embodied self, enveloping its knowledge.
meaningsTe: The senses, the mind, and
the intellect are said to be
its instruments; by these, it overpowers
the embodied self, enveloping its knowledge.

meaningsEn: Therefore
O Arjuna
control your senses from the outset and slay
this sinful thing that destroys both knowledge and discernment.
meaningsTe: Therefore
O Arjuna
control your senses from the outset and slay
this sinful thing that destroys both knowledge and discernment.

meaningsEn: They say that the senses are high
the mind is higher than the senses
the intellect is higher than the mind
but what is greater than the intellect is that (desire).
meaningsTe: They say that the senses are high
the mind is higher than the senses
the intellect is higher than the mind
but what is greater than the intellect is that (desire).

meaningsEn: Thus, knowing that which is higher than the intellect
and fixing the mind with the help of the intellect
in Karma Yoga, O Arjuna, slay this enemy which takes
the form of desire, and which is difficult to overcome.
meaningsTe: Thus, knowing that which is higher than the intellect
and fixing the mind with the help of the intellect
in Karma Yoga, O Arjuna, slay this enemy which takes
the form of desire, and which is difficult to overcome.

meaningsEn: There is a banyan tree with roots
above and branches below. Its leaves
are the Vedic hymns. One who
understands this tree knows the Vedas.
meaningsTe: పైకి వేర్లు మరియు క్రిందికి
కొమ్మలు ఉన్న అశ్వత్థ వృక్షం
ఉంది. దాని ఆకులు వేదాలు.
దాన్ని తెలిసినవాడు వేదాలను తెలిసినవాడే.

meaningsEn: The branches extend upward and downward
nourished by the three
qualities. The roots spread downward
binding humans through actions.
meaningsTe: ఈ చెట్టు
కొమ్మలు పైకి క్రిందికి
వ్యాపించి ఉంటాయి. వేర్లు
కర్మలతో మనుషులను కట్టిపడేస్తాయి.

lines: nānto na chādir na cha sampratiṣhṭhā
meaningsEn: This tree’s form is not
easily understood. It has no beginning
or end. Cut this deeply rooted
tree with the weapon of detachment.
meaningsTe: ఈ చెట్టు రూపం
సులభంగా అర్థం కాదు. దీనికి
ఆది అంతం లేదు. అసక్తి
అనే ఆయుధంతో దీనిని కోయాలి.

meaningsEn: One must search for that supreme state
reaching which one never returns. Surrender to
that original Supreme Person
from whom everything began.
meaningsTe: ఎవరైనా చేరిన తర్వాత
తిరిగి రాని ఆ పరమపదాన్ని
అన్వేషించాలి. అన్నింటి ఆది అయిన
ఆ పరమాత్మునికి శరణు పొందాలి.

meaningsEn: Those free from ego and illusion
who have overcome attachment and desires
and are balanced in happiness and sorrow
reach the eternal state.
meaningsTe: అహంకారం, మోహం,
ఆసక్తి, కోరికల నుండి విముక్తి పొంది,
సుఖదుఃఖాలలో సమత్వంతో ఉన్నవారు ఆ శాశ్వత స్థితిని చేరుతారు.

meaningsEn: That supreme abode is not illuminated by the sun
moon
or fire. Having reached it
one never returns.
meaningsTe: ఆ పరమధామాన్ని సూర్యుడు
చంద్రుడు
అగ్ని ప్రకాశింపజేయవు. దాన్ని
చేరినవారు తిరిగి రారు.

meaningsEn: The living beings are eternal parts of Me
but they struggle with the six
senses including the
mind in material nature.
meaningsTe: ప్రతి జీవి నా
శాశ్వత భాగమే. కానీ
అది మనస్సుతో కూడిన
ఇంద్రియాలతో ప్రకృతిలో పోరాడుతుంది.

meaningsEn: When the soul accepts a body and when it leaves it
it takes the mind and senses along
just as the wind
carries fragrances from their source.
meaningsTe: జీవాత్మ ఒక శరీరాన్ని
స్వీకరించినప్పుడు మరియు దాన్ని విడిచినప్పుడు
అది మనస్సు మరియు ఇంద్రియాలను వెంట తీసుకెళ్తుంది
గాలి వాసనను తీసుకెళ్లినట్లు.

meaningsEn: The soul uses the ears, eyes,
skin, tongue, and nose, along
with the mind, to experience
the objects of the world.
meaningsTe: జీవాత్మ మనస్సుతో కలిసి చెవులు, కళ్ళు,
చర్మం, నాలుక,
ముక్కు ద్వారా ప్రపంచాన్ని అనుభవిస్తుంది.

meaningsEn: The ignorant cannot perceive
the soul as it leaves
or stays in the body or enjoys through the senses
but those with knowledge can see it.
meaningsTe: ఆత్మ శరీరాన్ని విడిచినా
ఉండినా
అనుభవించినా అజ్ఞానులు గ్రహించలేరు
కానీ జ్ఞానులు దాన్ని తెలుసుకుంటారు.

meaningsEn: The striving yogīs see this (Supreme Lord) established within
themselves. But those who are unrefined and lack discrimination
though striving
do not see Him.
meaningsTe: ప్రయత్నించే యోగులు దీనిని (పరమాత్మను)
తమలోనే స్థితమై ఉండడం చూస్తారు. ప్రయత్నించినా
అపరిపక్వమైన మనస్సు గలవారు
వివేకం లేనివారు దీనిని చూడలేరు.

meaningsEn: The radiance that resides in the
sun and illuminates the entire world
that which is in the moon and
in fire—know that radiance to be Mine.
meaningsTe: సూర్యునిలో ఉండి సమస్త
జగత్తును ప్రకాశింపజేసే తేజస్సు
చంద్రునిలోని తేజస్సు
అగ్నిలోని తేజస్సు - ఆ తేజస్సు నాది అని తెలుసుకో.

meaningsEn: Entering the earth
I support all beings with
My energy. Becoming the moon (Soma)
I nourish all herbs with the essence of juice.
meaningsTe: భూమిలో ప్రవేశించి
నేను నా శక్తితో సమస్త
ప్రాణులను ధరిస్తాను. సోముడినై (చంద్రుడినై) రసాత్మకుడినై
సమస్త ఔషధులను పోషిస్తాను.

meaningsEn: Becoming the fire Vaiśvānara (digestive fire) and
abiding in the body of living beings
associated with prāṇa (incoming breath) and apāna (outgoing breath)
I digest the four kinds of food.
meaningsTe: నేను వైశ్వానరుడనై (జఠరాగ్నినై)
ప్రాణుల దేహంలో ప్రవేశించి
ప్రాణాపానాలతో కూడి
నాలుగు రకాల ఆహారాన్ని జీర్ణం చేస్తాను.

lines: vedaiśh cha sarvair aham eva vedyo
meaningsEn: And I am situated in the heart of everyone.
From Me come memory, knowledge, and their loss.
I alone am to be known by all the Vedas.
I am the author of Vedānta, and the knower of the Vedas I am.
meaningsTe: నేను అందరి హృదయంలోనూ ఉన్నాను.
నా నుండే జ్ఞాపకం, జ్ఞానం, వాటి నాశనం కలుగుతాయి.
అన్ని వేదాలకు నేనే తెలియదగినవాడిని.
వేదాంతాన్ని చెప్పినవాడను, వేదాలను తెలిసినవాడను నేనే.

meaningsEn: There are two Puruṣas (beings) in the world
the Kṣara (perishable) and the Akṣara (imperishable). The Kṣara is
all beings (material bodies). The
Kūṭastha (unchanging) is called the Akṣara
meaningsTe: ఈ లోకంలో రెండు పురుషులు ఉన్నారు
క్షరుడు (నాశనం అయ్యేవాడు) మరియు అక్షరుడు (నాశనం లేనివాడు). క్షరుడు
అంటే సమస్త ప్రాణులు (శరీరాలు).
అక్షరుడు అంటే కూటస్థుడు (మార్పులేనివాడు)

meaningsEn: But distinct is the Supreme
Puruṣa (Puruṣottama), called the Paramātmā,
who, entering the three worlds,
sustains them, the imperishable Lord.
meaningsTe: అయితే వేరే ఉత్తమ పురుషుడు (పురుషోత్తముడు) ఉన్నాడు. ఆయన పరమాత్మ
అని చెప్పబడ్డాడు. ఆయన మూడు లోకాలలోకి ప్రవేశించి వాటిని ధరిస్తాడు
అవ్యయుడు
ఈశ్వరుడు.

meaningsEn: Because I transcend the perishable (Kṣara) and
am even higher than the imperishable (Akṣara)
therefore in the world and in the Vedas
I am renowned as Puruṣottama (the Supreme Being).
meaningsTe: నేను క్షరునికి అతీతుడిని
అక్షరునికంటే కూడా ఉత్తముడిని కాబట్టి
లోకంలోను
వేదంలోను నేను పురుషోత్తముడిగా ప్రసిద్ధుడిని.

meaningsEn: He who, free from delusion, knows
Me thus as the Supreme Being
(Puruṣottama), knows everything, O Arjuna, and
worships Me with his whole being.
meaningsTe: ఎవడు ఈ విధంగా మోహం లేకుండా నన్ను పురుషోత్తమునిగా తెలుసుకుంటాడో
అతడు అంతటినీ తెలిసినవాడు
ఓ అర్జునా
మరియు సమస్త భావంతో నన్ను భజిస్తాడు.

meaningsEn: Thus this most secret scripture has been spoken by Me
O sinless one. Knowing this
one becomes wise and achieves all that is to be done
O Arjuna.
meaningsTe: ఈ విధంగా అతి రహస్యమైన శాస్త్రం నా చేత చెప్పబడింది
ఓ పాపరహితుడా (అర్జునా). దీనిని తెలుసుకుని
మనిషి బుద్ధిమంతుడు అవుతాడు
మరియు కృతకృత్యుడు అవుతాడు.

meaningsEn: The Lord said
"I taught this imperishable
Yoga to Vivasvan; Vivasvan
taught it to Manu; Manu declared it to Iksvaku."
meaningsTe: The Lord said
"I taught this imperishable
Yoga to Vivasvan; Vivasvan
taught it to Manu; Manu declared it to Iksvaku."

meaningsEn: Thus handed down in succession
the royal sages knew this (Karma Yoga). But with a long lapse of time
O Arjuna
that Yoga was lost to the world.
meaningsTe: Thus handed down in succession
the royal sages knew this (Karma Yoga). But with a long lapse of time
O Arjuna
that Yoga was lost to the world.

meaningsEn: It is the same ancient Yoga
that I am now teaching you
for you are My devotee and My friend. For
this is a supreme mystery.
meaningsTe: It is the same ancient Yoga
that I am now teaching you
for you are My devotee and My friend. For
this is a supreme mystery.

meaningsEn: Your birth was later
and Vivasvan's birth was earlier. How then can
I understand that you
taught it in the beginning?"
meaningsTe: Your birth was later
and Vivasvan's birth was earlier. How then can
I understand that you
taught it in the beginning?"

meaningsEn: The Lord said, "Many of My
births have passed, O Arjuna, as
have yours. I know them all,
but you do not know them."
meaningsTe: The Lord said, "Many of My
births have passed, O Arjuna, as
have yours. I know them all,
but you do not know them."

meaningsEn: Though I am birthless and of immutable nature
and the Lord of all beings
yet by employing My own Nature (Prakrti)
I am born out of My own free will.
meaningsTe: Though I am birthless and of immutable nature
and the Lord of all beings
yet by employing My own Nature (Prakrti)
I am born out of My own free will.

meaningsEn: Whenever there is a decline of Dharma
O Arjuna
and an uprising of Adharma
then I incarnate myself.
meaningsTe: Whenever there is a decline of Dharma
O Arjuna
and an uprising of Adharma
then I incarnate myself.

meaningsEn: For the protection of the good
and the destruction of the wicked
for the establishment of Dharma
I am born from age to age.
meaningsTe: For the protection of the good
and the destruction of the wicked
for the establishment of Dharma
I am born from age to age.

meaningsEn: He who thus knows in truth
My divine birth and actions does
not get rebirth after leaving the body; he will come to Me
O Arjuna.
meaningsTe: He who thus knows in truth
My divine birth and actions does
not get rebirth after leaving the body; he will come to Me
O Arjuna.

meaningsEn: Freed from desire, fear, and
wrath, absorbed in Me, depending upon
Me, purified by the austerity of
knowledge, many have attained My state.
meaningsTe: Freed from desire, fear, and
wrath, absorbed in Me, depending upon
Me, purified by the austerity of
knowledge, many have attained My state.

meaningsEn: Whoever resorts to Me in any manner
I favor them in the same manner;
men experience Me alone in different ways
O Arjuna.
meaningsTe: Whoever resorts to Me in any manner
I favor them in the same manner;
men experience Me alone in different ways
O Arjuna.

meaningsEn: Those who desire the
fruits of their ritualistic acts
sacrifice to the gods here; for
success quickly accrues in the world of men.
meaningsTe: Those who desire the
fruits of their ritualistic acts
sacrifice to the gods here; for
success quickly accrues in the world of men.

meaningsEn: The system of four stations was created by Me
according to the distinction of Gunas
and Karma. Though I am their creator
know Me to be non-agent and immutable.
meaningsTe: The system of four stations was created by Me
according to the distinction of Gunas
and Karma. Though I am their creator
know Me to be non-agent and immutable.

meaningsEn: Works cannot contaminate Me. There is
no desire for the fruits of
actions in Me. He who understands
this is not bound by actions.
meaningsTe: Works cannot contaminate Me. There is
no desire for the fruits of
actions in Me. He who understands
this is not bound by actions.

meaningsEn: Knowing thus
even ancient seekers of
liberation did their work. Therefore
do your work only as the ancients did in olden times.
meaningsTe: Knowing thus
even ancient seekers of
liberation did their work. Therefore
do your work only as the ancients did in olden times.

meaningsEn: What is action?
What is non-action?
Even the wise are puzzled in respect of these.
I shall declare to you that kind of action, knowing which you will be freed from evil.
meaningsTe: What is action?
What is non-action?
Even the wise are puzzled in respect of these.
I shall declare to you that kind of action, knowing which you will be freed from evil.

meaningsEn: For
there is what ought to be known in action; likewise
there is what ought to be known in multi-form action; and there is what ought to be understood in non-action. Thus
mysterious is the way of action.
meaningsTe: For
there is what ought to be known in action; likewise
there is what ought to be known in multi-form action; and there is what ought to be understood in non-action. Thus
mysterious is the way of action.

meaningsEn: He who sees inaction in action and
also action in inaction is wise
among men. He is fit for
release and has accomplished all actions.
meaningsTe: He who sees inaction in action and
also action in inaction is wise
among men. He is fit for
release and has accomplished all actions.

meaningsEn: He whose every undertaking is free from desire
and delusive identification (of the body with the self)
whose actions are burned up in the fire
of knowledge—the wise describe him as a sage.
meaningsTe: He whose every undertaking is free from desire
and delusive identification (of the body with the self)
whose actions are burned up in the fire
of knowledge—the wise describe him as a sage.

meaningsEn: Having renounced attachment to the fruits of
their actions, ever contented with the eternal self,
and dependent on none, one does not act
at all, even while being engaged in action.
meaningsTe: Having renounced attachment to the fruits of
their actions, ever contented with the eternal self,
and dependent on none, one does not act
at all, even while being engaged in action.

meaningsEn: Free from desire, his intellect and
mind controlled, having given up all
possessions, and doing bodily work only,
he is not subject to evil.
meaningsTe: Free from desire, his intellect and
mind controlled, having given up all
possessions, and doing bodily work only,
he is not subject to evil.

meaningsEn: Content with what chance may bring, rising
above the pairs of opposites, free from
ill will, even minded in success and
failure, he acts, yet is not bound.
meaningsTe: Content with what chance may bring, rising
above the pairs of opposites, free from
ill will, even minded in success and
failure, he acts, yet is not bound.

meaningsEn: One whose attachments have been relinquished
who is liberated
whose mind is established in knowledge
and who works only for sacrifices—their Karma is entirely dissolved.
meaningsTe: One whose attachments have been relinquished
who is liberated
whose mind is established in knowledge
and who works only for sacrifices—their Karma is entirely dissolved.

meaningsEn: Brahman is the instrument with which to offer; Brahman
is the oblation. By Brahman is the oblation offered
into the fire of Brahman; Brahman alone is to be
attained by one who meditates on Him in their works.
meaningsTe: Brahman is the instrument with which to offer; Brahman
is the oblation. By Brahman is the oblation offered
into the fire of Brahman; Brahman alone is to be
attained by one who meditates on Him in their works.

meaningsEn: Some yogis resort only to the
sacrifice relating to gods; others
offer sacrifice into the fire
of Brahman solely through sacrifice.
meaningsTe: Some yogis resort only to the
sacrifice relating to gods; others
offer sacrifice into the fire
of Brahman solely through sacrifice.

meaningsEn: Others offer as oblations hearing and other senses into the fires
of restraint. Some others offer as oblations the objects of the senses
such as sound and the rest
into the fires of their senses.
meaningsTe: Others offer as oblations hearing and other senses into the fires
of restraint. Some others offer as oblations the objects of the senses
such as sound and the rest
into the fires of their senses.

meaningsEn: Some again offer as an oblation the
functions of the senses and the activity
of the vital breaths into the fire of the Yoga of restraint of the mind
kindled by knowledge.
meaningsTe: Some again offer as an oblation the
functions of the senses and the activity
of the vital breaths into the fire of the Yoga of restraint of the mind
kindled by knowledge.

meaningsEn: Self-controlled and firm of resolve
others perform the sacrifice of material objects or austerities
or yoga; while others offer
their scriptural study and knowledge.
meaningsTe: Self-controlled and firm of resolve
others perform the sacrifice of material objects or austerities
or yoga; while others offer
their scriptural study and knowledge.

meaningsEn: Others, with restricted diets, are devoted to the control of breath. Some
sacrifice the inward breath in the outward breath; similarly, others sacrifice the
outward breath in the inward breath. Some others, stopping the flow of
both the inward and outward breaths, sacrifice the inward and outward breaths.
meaningsTe: Others, with restricted diets, are devoted to the control of breath. Some
sacrifice the inward breath in the outward breath; similarly, others sacrifice the
outward breath in the inward breath. Some others, stopping the flow of
both the inward and outward breaths, sacrifice the inward and outward breaths.

meaningsEn: All these know the meaning of sacrifices, and
through sacrifices, their sins are eradicated. Those
who subsist on the ambrosial food, the
remnants of sacrifices, go to eternal Brahman.
meaningsTe: All these know the meaning of sacrifices, and
through sacrifices, their sins are eradicated. Those
who subsist on the ambrosial food, the
remnants of sacrifices, go to eternal Brahman.

meaningsEn: This world is not for one who
makes no sacrifice; how
then for the other
O Arjuna?
meaningsTe: This world is not for one who
makes no sacrifice; how
then for the other
O Arjuna?

meaningsEn: Thus
many forms of sacrifices have been spread out as means of reaching Brahman (individual self
in its own nature). Know that all of these are born of actions. Knowing thus
you will be free.
meaningsTe: Thus
many forms of sacrifices have been spread out as means of reaching Brahman (individual self
in its own nature). Know that all of these are born of actions. Knowing thus
you will be free.

meaningsEn: The sacrifice of knowledge is
superior to material sacrifice. O Arjuna
all actions and everything
else culminate in knowledge.
meaningsTe: The sacrifice of knowledge is
superior to material sacrifice. O Arjuna
all actions and everything
else culminate in knowledge.

meaningsEn: Know this through prostration
questioning
and service. The wise who have realized
the truth will instruct you in knowledge.
meaningsTe: Know this through prostration
questioning
and service. The wise who have realized
the truth will instruct you in knowledge.

meaningsEn: Knowing this
O Arjuna
you will not fall again into delusion in this way—by that knowledge
you will see all beings without exception in yourself and then in Me.
meaningsTe: Knowing this
O Arjuna
you will not fall again into delusion in this way—by that knowledge
you will see all beings without exception in yourself and then in Me.

meaningsEn: Even if you are the
most sinful of all sinners
you can cross over all sins
by the boat of knowledge alone.
meaningsTe: Even if you are the
most sinful of all sinners
you can cross over all sins
by the boat of knowledge alone.

meaningsEn: Just as a burning fire turns fuel to ashes
O Arjuna
so does the fire of
knowledge turn all karmas to ashes.
meaningsTe: Just as a burning fire turns fuel to ashes
O Arjuna
so does the fire of
knowledge turn all karmas to ashes.

meaningsEn: For there is no purifier equal
to knowledge; he who is perfected in
Karma Yoga finds this knowledge of his
own accord in himself in due time.
meaningsTe: For there is no purifier equal
to knowledge; he who is perfected in
Karma Yoga finds this knowledge of his
own accord in himself in due time.

meaningsEn: He who has faith, is intent
on it, and has mastered his
senses, attains knowledge. Having attained knowledge,
he quickly goes to supreme peace.
meaningsTe: He who has faith, is intent
on it, and has mastered his
senses, attains knowledge. Having attained knowledge,
he quickly goes to supreme peace.

meaningsEn: The ignorant, the faithless, and the
doubting one perish; for the doubting
one, there is neither this world
nor the one beyond, nor happiness.
meaningsTe: The ignorant, the faithless, and the
doubting one perish; for the doubting
one, there is neither this world
nor the one beyond, nor happiness.

meaningsEn: Actions do not bind him
O Arjuna
who has renounced them through Karma Yoga and whose doubts have been dispelled by knowledge
and who thus possesses a steady mind.
meaningsTe: Actions do not bind him
O Arjuna
who has renounced them through Karma Yoga and whose doubts have been dispelled by knowledge
and who thus possesses a steady mind.

meaningsEn: Therefore, sever, with the sword of
knowledge, this doubt present in your
heart resulting from ignorance concerning the Self.
Practice this Yoga, O Arjuna, and arise.
meaningsTe: Therefore, sever, with the sword of
knowledge, this doubt present in your
heart resulting from ignorance concerning the Self.
Practice this Yoga, O Arjuna, and arise.

meaningsEn: you praise the renunciation of actions
and then you also praise Karma Yoga. Please tell
me with certainty which of these is the superior one
leading to the ultimate good.
meaningsTe: you praise the renunciation of actions
and then you also praise Karma Yoga. Please tell
me with certainty which of these is the superior one
leading to the ultimate good.

meaningsEn: The Lord said
"Renunciation of actions and Karma Yoga both lead to the highest excellence; however
of the two
Karma Yoga surpasses renunciation of actions."
meaningsTe: The Lord said
"Renunciation of actions and Karma Yoga both lead to the highest excellence; however
of the two
Karma Yoga surpasses renunciation of actions."

meaningsEn: He who neither hates nor desires, and
is beyond the pairs of opposites, is to
be understood as an ever renouncer. Therefore, he
is easily set free from bondage, O Arjuna.
meaningsTe: He who neither hates nor desires, and
is beyond the pairs of opposites, is to
be understood as an ever renouncer. Therefore, he
is easily set free from bondage, O Arjuna.

meaningsEn: Children, not the learned, speak of
Sankhya and Yoga as distinct; however,
he who is firmly set in
one, attains the fruit of both.
meaningsTe: Children, not the learned, speak of
Sankhya and Yoga as distinct; however,
he who is firmly set in
one, attains the fruit of both.

meaningsEn: That state which is reached by the Sankhyans
the same is also attained by the Yogins; that is
the same state is achieved by those who are Karma Yogins. He alone is wise who perceives that the Sankhya and the Yoga are one and the same
due to their having the same result.
meaningsTe: That state which is reached by the Sankhyans
the same is also attained by the Yogins; that is
the same state is achieved by those who are Karma Yogins. He alone is wise who perceives that the Sankhya and the Yoga are one and the same
due to their having the same result.

meaningsEn: But
O mighty-armed one
renunciation is hard to attain without practicing Yoga. The sage who
contemplates and follows Yoga soon reaches the Brahman (the self or Atman).
meaningsTe: But
O mighty-armed one
renunciation is hard to attain without practicing Yoga. The sage who
contemplates and follows Yoga soon reaches the Brahman (the self or Atman).

meaningsEn: He who follows the Yoga and is pure in mind,
who has subdued his self and has conquered his
senses, and whose self has become the self of
all beings, even while he is acting, remains untainted.
meaningsTe: He who follows the Yoga and is pure in mind,
who has subdued his self and has conquered his
senses, and whose self has become the self of
all beings, even while he is acting, remains untainted.

lines: naiva kiñchit karomīti yukto manyeta tattva-vit
pralapan visṛijan gṛihṇann unmiṣhan nimiṣhann api
meaningsEn: The one who knows the truth and
is devoted to yoga should think, "I am
not doing anything," even though they are seeing,
hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, and breathing.
meaningsTe: The one who knows the truth and
is devoted to yoga should think, "I am
not doing anything," even though they are seeing,
hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, and breathing.

meaningsEn: Speaking, discharging, grasping, opening, and
closing his eyes, etc., he
should always bear in mind that
the senses operate among sense objects.
meaningsTe: Speaking, discharging, grasping, opening, and
closing his eyes, etc., he
should always bear in mind that
the senses operate among sense objects.

meaningsEn: He who acts without attachment
reposing all actions on Brahman (Prakṛti)
is untouched by evil
just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
meaningsTe: He who acts without attachment
reposing all actions on Brahman (Prakṛti)
is untouched by evil
just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.

meaningsEn: Yogins, renouncing attachment, do
actions with merely the body,
mind, intellect, and senses, for
the purification of the self.
meaningsTe: Yogins, renouncing attachment, do
actions with merely the body,
mind, intellect, and senses, for
the purification of the self.

meaningsEn: A yogi, renouncing the fruits of their
actions, attains lasting peace. But the unsteady
person who is attached to the fruits of
their actions, being driven by desire, is bound.
meaningsTe: A yogi, renouncing the fruits of their
actions, attains lasting peace. But the unsteady
person who is attached to the fruits of
their actions, being driven by desire, is bound.

meaningsEn: The embodied self, mentally resigning all actions as belonging
to the city of nine gates (i.e., the
body) and becoming self controlled, dwells happily, neither
acting himself nor causing the body to act.
meaningsTe: The embodied self, mentally resigning all actions as belonging
to the city of nine gates (i.e., the
body) and becoming self controlled, dwells happily, neither
acting himself nor causing the body to act.

meaningsEn: The Lord of the body (the Self, i.e.,
the Jiva) does not create agency, nor actions, nor
union with the fruits of actions in relation to
the world of selves; only the inherent tendencies function.
meaningsTe: The Lord of the body (the Self, i.e.,
the Jiva) does not create agency, nor actions, nor
union with the fruits of actions in relation to
the world of selves; only the inherent tendencies function.

meaningsEn: The all pervasive One takes away neither the sin
nor the merit of anyone.
Knowledge is enveloped by ignorance
and creatures are thereby deluded.
meaningsTe: The all pervasive One takes away neither the sin
nor the merit of anyone.
Knowledge is enveloped by ignorance
and creatures are thereby deluded.

meaningsEn: But for those in whom this ignorance is destroyed by the knowledge of the Self
that knowledge
in their case
is supreme and shines brightly like the sun.
meaningsTe: But for those in whom this ignorance is destroyed by the knowledge of the Self
that knowledge
in their case
is supreme and shines brightly like the sun.

meaningsEn: Those whose intellects pursue it, whose minds think about it,
who undergo discipline for it, and who hold it
as their highest object, have their impurities cleansed by
knowledge and go from whence there is no return.
meaningsTe: Those whose intellects pursue it, whose minds think about it,
who undergo discipline for it, and who hold it
as their highest object, have their impurities cleansed by
knowledge and go from whence there is no return.

meaningsEn: The sages look with an equal
eye on one endowed with learning
and humility, a Brahmana, a cow, an
elephant, a dog, and a dog eater.
meaningsTe: The sages look with an equal
eye on one endowed with learning
and humility, a Brahmana, a cow, an
elephant, a dog, and a dog eater.

meaningsEn: Here itself, those whose minds rest in
equanimity overcome samsara. For the Brahman (individual
self), when uncontaminated by Prakriti, is the
same everywhere; therefore, they abide in Brahman.
meaningsTe: Here itself, those whose minds rest in
equanimity overcome samsara. For the Brahman (individual
self), when uncontaminated by Prakriti, is the
same everywhere; therefore, they abide in Brahman.

meaningsEn: He who knows Brahman (individual self) and abides in Brahman
whose mind is steadfastly focused on the self and undeluded by body consciousness—he
neither rejoices at gaining what is pleasant
nor grieves on obtaining what is unpleasant.
meaningsTe: He who knows Brahman (individual self) and abides in Brahman
whose mind is steadfastly focused on the self and undeluded by body consciousness—he
neither rejoices at gaining what is pleasant
nor grieves on obtaining what is unpleasant.

meaningsEn: He whose mind is detached from
external contact and finds happiness in the
Self—he has his mind engaged in the
contemplation of Brahman and enjoys undecaying bliss.
meaningsTe: He whose mind is detached from
external contact and finds happiness in the
Self—he has his mind engaged in the
contemplation of Brahman and enjoys undecaying bliss.

meaningsEn: For those pleasures that
are born of contact are
wombs of pain. They have a beginning and an end
O Arjuna; the wise do not rejoice in them.
meaningsTe: For those pleasures that
are born of contact are
wombs of pain. They have a beginning and an end
O Arjuna; the wise do not rejoice in them.

meaningsEn: He who is able, even here, before being
released from the body, to bear the impulse
generated by desire and anger, he is a Yogin
(competent for self realisation); he is the happy man.
meaningsTe: He who is able, even here, before being
released from the body, to bear the impulse
generated by desire and anger, he is a Yogin
(competent for self realisation); he is the happy man.

meaningsEn: He whose joy is within, whose
pleasure is within, and whose light
is within—he is a yogin, who, having
become Brahman, attains the bliss of Brahman.
meaningsTe: He whose joy is within, whose
pleasure is within, and whose light
is within—he is a yogin, who, having
become Brahman, attains the bliss of Brahman.

meaningsEn: The sages, who are free from the pairs of
opposites, whose minds are well subdued, and who are
devoted to the welfare of all beings, become cleansed
of all impurities and attain the bliss of Brahman.
meaningsTe: The sages, who are free from the pairs of
opposites, whose minds are well subdued, and who are
devoted to the welfare of all beings, become cleansed
of all impurities and attain the bliss of Brahman.

meaningsEn: To those who are free from desire and wrath
who are accustomed to exerting themselves
whose thoughts are controlled
and who have conquered it—the beatitude of Brahman is close at hand.
meaningsTe: To those who are free from desire and wrath
who are accustomed to exerting themselves
whose thoughts are controlled
and who have conquered it—the beatitude of Brahman is close at hand.

lines: sparśhān kṛitvā bahir bāhyānśh chakṣhuśh chaivāntare bhruvoḥ
vigatechchhā-bhaya-krodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ
meaningsEn: Shutting off outward contacts
fixing the gaze between the eyebrows
realizing inward and outward
breaths moving in the nostrils;
meaningsTe: Shutting off outward contacts
fixing the gaze between the eyebrows
realizing inward and outward
breaths moving in the nostrils;

meaningsEn: The sage who has controlled his senses,
mind, and intellect, who is intent on
release as his final goal, freed forever from
desire, fear, and wrath, is indeed liberated forever.
meaningsTe: The sage who has controlled his senses,
mind, and intellect, who is intent on
release as his final goal, freed forever from
desire, fear, and wrath, is indeed liberated forever.

meaningsEn: Knowing Me as the enjoyer of all sacrifices and austerities
as the Supreme Lord of all worlds
as the Friend of every being
he attains peace.
meaningsTe: Knowing Me as the enjoyer of all sacrifices and austerities
as the Supreme Lord of all worlds
as the Friend of every being
he attains peace.

meaningsEn: The Lord said
"He who performs works that ought to be done
without seeking their fruits—he is a sannyasin and yogin
and not he who maintains no sacred fires and performs no actions."
meaningsTe: The Lord said
"He who performs works that ought to be done
without seeking their fruits—he is a sannyasin and yogin
and not he who maintains no sacred fires and performs no actions."

meaningsEn: That which is called Sannyasa (Jnana Yoga), know that to
be Yoga (Karma Yoga), O Arjuna. For no one, among
Karma Yogins, whose delusive identification of the body with the
self has not been abandoned, becomes a true Karma Yogin.
meaningsTe: That which is called Sannyasa (Jnana Yoga), know that to
be Yoga (Karma Yoga), O Arjuna. For no one, among
Karma Yogins, whose delusive identification of the body with the
self has not been abandoned, becomes a true Karma Yogin.

meaningsEn: Action is said to be the means for the sage who seeks to
climb the heights of Yoga; but when
he has climbed the heights of Yoga
tranquility is said to be the means.
meaningsTe: Action is said to be the means for the sage who seeks to
climb the heights of Yoga; but when
he has climbed the heights of Yoga
tranquility is said to be the means.

meaningsEn: For
when one loses attachment to the things of the senses and to actions
then they have abandoned all desires and are
said to have climbed the heights of Yoga.
meaningsTe: For
when one loses attachment to the things of the senses and to actions
then they have abandoned all desires and are
said to have climbed the heights of Yoga.

meaningsEn: One should raise oneself by one's
own mind and not allow oneself
to sink; for the mind alone is the friend of the self
and the mind alone is the foe of the self.
meaningsTe: One should raise oneself by one's
own mind and not allow oneself
to sink; for the mind alone is the friend of the self
and the mind alone is the foe of the self.

meaningsEn: The mind is the friend of him by whom it has been conquered. But for him whose mind is not conquered
the mind
like an enemy
remains hostile.
meaningsTe: The mind is the friend of him by whom it has been conquered. But for him whose mind is not conquered
the mind
like an enemy
remains hostile.

meaningsEn: Of him whose mind is conquered and who is serene
the great self is well-secured in heat and cold
in pleasure and pain
and in honor and dishonor.
meaningsTe: Of him whose mind is conquered and who is serene
the great self is well-secured in heat and cold
in pleasure and pain
and in honor and dishonor.

meaningsEn: The yogin whose mind is content with knowledge of the self
and also with knowledge of the difference between the self and
Prakrti, who is established in the self, whose senses are subdued, and
to whom earth, stone, and gold all seem alike, is called integrated.
meaningsTe: The yogin whose mind is content with knowledge of the self
and also with knowledge of the difference between the self and
Prakrti, who is established in the self, whose senses are subdued, and
to whom earth, stone, and gold all seem alike, is called integrated.

meaningsEn: He who regards with an equal
eye well wishers, friends, foes, the
indifferent, neutrals, the hateful, the relations, and
even the good and the sinful—he excels.
meaningsTe: He who regards with an equal
eye well wishers, friends, foes, the
indifferent, neutrals, the hateful, the relations, and
even the good and the sinful—he excels.

meaningsEn: The yogin should constantly fix his mind on yoga
remaining in a solitary place all alone
controlling his thoughts and mind
free from desire and a sense of possession.
meaningsTe: The yogin should constantly fix his mind on yoga
remaining in a solitary place all alone
controlling his thoughts and mind
free from desire and a sense of possession.

meaningsEn: Having established for himself, in a clean spot,
a firm seat that is neither too high
nor too low, and covering it with cloth,
deer skin, and Kusa grass in reverse order—
meaningsTe: Having established for himself, in a clean spot,
a firm seat that is neither too high
nor too low, and covering it with cloth,
deer skin, and Kusa grass in reverse order—

meaningsEn: Sitting on the seat
with a concentrated mind
controlling the mind and senses
one should practice Yoga for the purification of the self.
meaningsTe: Sitting on the seat
with a concentrated mind
controlling the mind and senses
one should practice Yoga for the purification of the self.

meaningsEn: Holding the trunk, head, and
neck erect, motionless and steady, gazing
at the tip of the nose
and not looking in any direction;
meaningsTe: Holding the trunk, head, and
neck erect, motionless and steady, gazing
at the tip of the nose
and not looking in any direction;

meaningsEn: Serene and fearless, firm in their
vow of celibacy, controlling their minds
and fixing their thoughts on Me, they
should sit in Yoga, intent on Me.
meaningsTe: Serene and fearless, firm in their
vow of celibacy, controlling their minds
and fixing their thoughts on Me, they
should sit in Yoga, intent on Me.

meaningsEn: Applying his mind in this way
the Yogin of controlled mind
ever attains the peace which is the
summit of beatitude and which abides in Me.
meaningsTe: Applying his mind in this way
the Yogin of controlled mind
ever attains the peace which is the
summit of beatitude and which abides in Me.

meaningsEn: Yoga is not for him who overeats,
nor for him who fasts excessively; not
for him, O Arjuna, who sleeps too much,
nor for him who stays awake too long.
meaningsTe: Yoga is not for him who overeats,
nor for him who fasts excessively; not
for him, O Arjuna, who sleeps too much,
nor for him who stays awake too long.

meaningsEn: Yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrows for
those who are temperate in food and recreation
temperate in their actions
and temperate in their sleep and wakefulness.
meaningsTe: Yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrows for
those who are temperate in food and recreation
temperate in their actions
and temperate in their sleep and wakefulness.

meaningsEn: When the subdued mind rests solely on the Self
then
free from all yearning for objects of desire
one is said to be fit for Yoga.
meaningsTe: When the subdued mind rests solely on the Self
then
free from all yearning for objects of desire
one is said to be fit for Yoga.

meaningsEn: A lamp does not flicker
in a windless place"—that is the
simile used for the tranquil mind
of a yogi who practices yoga.
meaningsTe: A lamp does not flicker
in a windless place"—that is the
simile used for the tranquil mind
of a yogi who practices yoga.

meaningsEn: Where the mind
controlled through the practice of Yoga
rests
and where one sees the Self by the Self and is delighted by the Self alone.
meaningsTe: Where the mind
controlled through the practice of Yoga
rests
and where one sees the Self by the Self and is delighted by the Self alone.

meaningsEn: Where one knows that infinite happiness which can be grasped
by the intellect but is beyond the reach of the senses
and is established in that condition
one does not swerve from it.
meaningsTe: Where one knows that infinite happiness which can be grasped
by the intellect but is beyond the reach of the senses
and is established in that condition
one does not swerve from it.

meaningsEn: Having gained it
one holds that there is no
greater gain; being established in it
one is not moved even by the heaviest sorrow.
meaningsTe: Having gained it
one holds that there is no
greater gain; being established in it
one is not moved even by the heaviest sorrow.

meaningsEn: Know this deliverance from association with
misery to be Yoga. This Yoga
must be practiced with determination and
with a mind free from despondency.
meaningsTe: Know this deliverance from association with
misery to be Yoga. This Yoga
must be practiced with determination and
with a mind free from despondency.

meaningsEn: Renouncing entirely all desires
born of volition and
restraining the mind from all
the senses on all sides,
meaningsTe: Renouncing entirely all desires
born of volition and
restraining the mind from all
the senses on all sides,

meaningsEn: Little by little
one should withdraw oneself from objects other than the self
with the help of the intellect held by firm resolution; and then one should think of nothing else
having fixed the mind upon the Self.
meaningsTe: Little by little
one should withdraw oneself from objects other than the self
with the help of the intellect held by firm resolution; and then one should think of nothing else
having fixed the mind upon the Self.

meaningsEn: Wherever the fickle
and unsteady mind wanders
one should subdue it and then bring it
back under the control of the self alone.
meaningsTe: Wherever the fickle
and unsteady mind wanders
one should subdue it and then bring it
back under the control of the self alone.

meaningsEn: For supreme happiness comes to the Yogin whose mind is at peace
who is free from evil
from whom Rajas has departed
and who has become the Brahman.
meaningsTe: For supreme happiness comes to the Yogin whose mind is at peace
who is free from evil
from whom Rajas has departed
and who has become the Brahman.

meaningsEn: Thus
devoting himself to the Yoga of the Self
freed from impurities
the yogin easily attains the supreme bliss of contact with the Brahman.
meaningsTe: Thus
devoting himself to the Yoga of the Self
freed from impurities
the yogin easily attains the supreme bliss of contact with the Brahman.

meaningsEn: He whose mind is fixed in Yoga
sees reality everywhere; he sees his
Self as abiding in all beings
and all beings in his Self.
meaningsTe: He whose mind is fixed in Yoga
sees reality everywhere; he sees his
Self as abiding in all beings
and all beings in his Self.

meaningsEn: To him who sees Me in every self and
every self in Me—I
am not lost to him
nor is he lost to Me.
meaningsTe: To him who sees Me in every self and
every self in Me—I
am not lost to him
nor is he lost to Me.

meaningsEn: The yogi who
fixed in oneness
worships Me dwelling in all beings—he abides in Me
no matter how he may live.
meaningsTe: The yogi who
fixed in oneness
worships Me dwelling in all beings—he abides in Me
no matter how he may live.

meaningsEn: He who, due to the similarity
of selves everywhere, sees pleasure or
pain as the same everywhere—that yogi,
O Arjuna, is considered the closest.
meaningsTe: He who, due to the similarity
of selves everywhere, sees pleasure or
pain as the same everywhere—that yogi,
O Arjuna, is considered the closest.

meaningsEn: this Yoga of reality
which You have declared
I do not see how it can be
steady due to the fickleness of the mind."
meaningsTe: this Yoga of reality
which You have declared
I do not see how it can be
steady due to the fickleness of the mind."

meaningsEn: For the mind is fickle,
O Krsna, impetuous, powerful, and stubborn;
I think that restraining it is
as difficult as restraining the wind.
meaningsTe: For the mind is fickle,
O Krsna, impetuous, powerful, and stubborn;
I think that restraining it is
as difficult as restraining the wind.

meaningsEn: The Lord said, "The mind is indeed hard
to subdue and fickle, O mighty armed one,
but, O son of Kunti, it can be brought
under control through practice and the exercise of dispassion."
meaningsTe: The Lord said, "The mind is indeed hard
to subdue and fickle, O mighty armed one,
but, O son of Kunti, it can be brought
under control through practice and the exercise of dispassion."

meaningsEn: In my opinion
Yoga is hard to attain by a person of an unrestrained mind; however
it can be attained through the right means by
one who strives for it and has a subdued mind.
meaningsTe: In my opinion
Yoga is hard to attain by a person of an unrestrained mind; however
it can be attained through the right means by
one who strives for it and has a subdued mind.

meaningsEn: If a person who is possessed of faith but has put
in only inadequate effort finds his mind wandering away from Yoga
and then fails to attain perfection—what way does he go
O Krishna?"
meaningsTe: If a person who is possessed of faith but has put
in only inadequate effort finds his mind wandering away from Yoga
and then fails to attain perfection—what way does he go
O Krishna?"

meaningsEn: Without any support, confused in the path leading
to the Brahman, and thus having fallen
from both, does he not perish, O
mighty armed one, like a rent cloud?
meaningsTe: Without any support, confused in the path leading
to the Brahman, and thus having fallen
from both, does he not perish, O
mighty armed one, like a rent cloud?

meaningsEn: O Krsna
you should altogether remove this doubt of mine
for there is no other
remover of this doubt than you.
meaningsTe: O Krsna
you should altogether remove this doubt of mine
